newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish journalists protest camera ban in court.
newsitem.headline: Turkish journalists protest camera ban in court.

text.p: Turkish reporters and cameramen on Wednesday protested a ban on cameras in an Istanbul court that hears sensitive cases of political violence, Anatolian news agency said.

The agency said television workers laid down their cameras in front of the Istanbul state security court to draw attention to the ban, introduced three days ago. Turkish reporters decided not to cover any of Wednesday's cases at the court, Anatolian said.
State security courts often hear cases against Kurdish rebels, armed Islamists and leftist urban guerrillas. They are are usually open to the media.
The state-run agency quoted a reporter as saying the ban was aimed at preventing coverage of any trial in a security scandal over alleged official links to death squads and crime gangs.
Around 10 policemen and security officials have been charged in connection with the scandal but no clear date for their trial has been set.
The affair came to light last November after a top police officer and a wanted gangster died in a car crash. A government MP travelling in the same car was injured.
